title: The Mayor's Cat
teaser: Duchess the cat has been catnapped. The ransom note arrived at exactly 4:00. Only one suspect could have got there in time.

booklet.briefing:
Mayor Priya Gill wants to build a bypass road around Cobbleford. Not everyone is pleased. On Wednesday her beloved cat, Duchess, vanished from the garden.

At exactly 4:00:00 pm, the doorbell camera at the Mayor's House filmed a gloved hand pushing a note through the letterbox: “STOP THE BYPASS OR YOU WON'T SEE DUCHESS AGAIN.” The hood and the angle hid the face.

Four villagers loudly oppose the bypass. Each was seen somewhere else shortly before or after 4:00. Get out the village map and do the sums.
rules: The note was delivered by the catnapper in person at exactly 4:00 pm.
Everyone walks at 80 metres a minute. A bicycle goes 250 metres a minute, but only on roads, not on footpaths.
Use the shortest route. No one in the village has a car available that afternoon (see the evidence).

suspects.name: Ada Finch
suspects.description: Runs the village shop and fears the bypass will take away passing trade.
suspects.motive: Started the 'Save Our High Street' petition.
suspects.statement: I was in the shop till gone four. I served old Mr. Lowe at about four minutes to.

suspects.name: Bert Lacey
suspects.role: Cellarman at the Plough pub, bell ringer
suspects.description: Looks after the pub's beer cellar. Rings the church bells on Wednesdays. Rides an old green bicycle.
suspects.motive: The bypass would take lorries, and their thirsty drivers, away from the Plough.
suspects.statement: I settled my tab at the Plough at 3:52 and walked straight to the church for bell practice. I got there a bit after four.

suspects.name: Cora Whitlow
suspects.description: Walks everywhere. Thinks the bypass will ruin the meadows.
suspects.motive: Chains herself to things in protest. Often.
suspects.statement: I was at the library returning books. Then I walked to the Mayor's House to complain, but I heard the news and turned round.

suspects.name: Amos Dawson
suspects.description: The bypass would cut his farm in two.
suspects.motive: Stands to lose his best field.
suspects.statement: I was on the farm all afternoon waiting for the vet. My tractor's in pieces at the garage.

evidence.title: The tower captain
evidence.body: “Bert signed in at 4:03, bit out of breath. His green bike was leaning on the church railings when I came out at six. It hadn't been there at quarter to four when I arrived.”

evidence.body:
Amos Dawson's tractor: engine removed for repair since Monday. Not drivable.

No other vehicles are registered to anyone at the farm.

evidence.title: Where Duchess was found
evidence.body:
Duchess was found, cross but unharmed, in a crate in the Plough's beer cellar, with a saucer of milk. Only the landlord and the cellarman have keys to the cellar; the landlord was away all week at his sister's.

White cat hairs were found in the wicker basket of Bert Lacey's green bicycle.

questions.prompt: Who took Duchess and sent the note?
questions.explanation: Bert is the only suspect who could be at the letterbox at 4:00, and only by bicycle. He claimed he walked, but his bike appeared at the church railings that afternoon. Duchess was in the cellar he holds the key to, and her white hairs were in his bike basket.
hints: Only one suspect can reach the letterbox, and only one way.
Bert says he walked. Did his bike stay at the pub?
Where was Duchess found, and what was in the bike basket?

solution.explanation: Bert Lacey scooped Duchess from the Mayor's garden that morning and hid her in the Plough's cellar. At 3:52 he settled his tab, jumped on his green bicycle, pedalled to the Mayor's House, pushed the note through the letterbox at 4:00 and raced on to the church, signing in at 4:03 a little out of breath. He told everyone he'd walked, but on foot the trip would have taken him twice as long.

chain.step: Ada can't arrive before 4:01, Cora before 4:01, or Dawson before about 4:07, and Dawson had no working vehicle.
Bert on foot needs over 21 minutes for pub to Mayor's House to church; he had 11.
By bicycle on roads it takes under 7 minutes, so he could deliver the note at 4:00 and sign in at 4:03.
His bike appeared at the church railings that afternoon, even though he says he walked.
Duchess was in the cellar he has a key to, and her hairs were in his bike basket.
